newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Thousands stage anti-government rally in Slovakia.
newsitem.headline: Thousands stage anti-government rally in Slovakia.

text.p: Thousands of Slovaks demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Thursday in a march through the capital Bratislava marked by a symbolic jangling of keys.

The crowd of roughly 10,000 chanted "Down with Meciar" and many shook keys in the air in a reminder of mass rallies of November, 1989 that spurred the collapse of the communist government in former Czechoslovakia.
The practice of mass key-ringing was used to symbolise a bell tolling for the end of the widely-loathed communist regime.

The rally, dubbed "Save Slovakia", was called by the newly-formed "Blue Coalition" of centrist and conservative opposition parties against what they called government moves to stifle freedom of culture and independent education.
The premier leads a three-party coalition government of nationalist and leftist parties.
Actor Matej Landl, a member of the "Save Culture" movement read a message of support from President Michal Kovac, the political arch-rival of Meciar.
"Our country is in our own hands," Kovac read. "It is sad that after seven years, the citizens of this country again have to raise their voices to call for justice and human rights."

Jan Carnogursky, head of the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH) and a former jailed dissident, told the rally: "Like in November 1989 people from all walks of life and culture have gathered here to protest against the installation of a new type of dictatorship,"
Kovac and Meciar have been locked in a bitter political battle since Kovac forced parliament to hold a vote of confidence in Meciar in the spring of 1984.

Meciar bounced back in the elections later that year and has since gradually stripped Kovac of many of his presidential powers. He and his political allies have called several times for Kovac's resignation.
However, Meciar lacks a three-fifths parliamentary majority needed to vote Kovac out office.
